Information since February points to continued labor‑market strength, moderate growth, and inflation trending toward 2%, supporting the 25 bp rate hike within an overall accommodative stance and ongoing balance-sheet reinvestments. Incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey: domestic banks reported C&I standards largely unchanged but expect to ease ahead amid stronger business loan demand, which supports investment. Offsetting this, banks expect tighter standards for CRE (including construction/land development) and auto loans, and foresee deteriorating asset quality in credit cards, auto, and multifamily; foreign banks report weaker business loan demand and plan tighter C&I/CRE standards. Mortgage standards are expected to be little changed for GSE‑eligible loans, with some improvement anticipated in nonconforming jumbo/subprime asset quality. Net effect: the credit channel is mixed—some support to business lending but caution in CRE and consumer credit—reinforcing the FOMC’s gradualism and data dependence and tempering the otherwise moderately positive tone.
